svg.aria-label: Sequence diagram: a node freezes in the middle of a put. The leader sees its registration unchanged for the departure time, moves its HELD entry to PENDING, aborts its uploads and finishes the entry. When the node wakes it is past its live_until, answers 503 and touches nothing; a late call that does land fails its compare-and-swap.
svg.title: A node freezes holding a key: how the leader reaps it, and what the node meets on waking
svg.text: A node freezes holding a key: how the leader reaps it, and what the node meets on waking
A node (frozen)
Hot tier
Leader
1 create entry (PUT, HELD, node A-4); heartbeat every 10 s
the node freezes
mid-upload: no more
heartbeats
2 scans: the registration of A-4 has not changed
for D = 60 s on the leader's own monotonic clock: departed
3 CAS entry (PUT, HELD, A-4) to (PUT, PENDING): reap
abort A-4's multipart uploads for the key (list_uploads)
4 PENDING step: hot object absent (never landed) means release;
present means replicate to cold. Delete the entry
The key was blocked for about D (503 to other puts of it) and is free again. The put was never acknowledged, so nothing is lost.
the node wakes
5 a step checks live_until (last heartbeat + D - m): past it,
the node answers 503 and never touches the entry or the data again
6 a call already on the wire still lands: its create-only write
is a valid late put, never acknowledged; its entry CAS finds a changed tag and
fails
What a frozen actor can still do is stated, not hidden: a late plain DELETE of data or of an entry (stores that ignore If-Match on DELETE), a
stalled leader's late cold publish, and a reaped client's late landing (section 11, R1 to R4). Each needs an actor frozen for longer than the
departure time.
